items_missed: 1_set_agenda: never asked the customer's name, never asked how she was doing, gave no agenda statement, and never got an explicit 'sound good?' confirmation

2_probe: never got the address/zip (origin or destination), stairs/floors, additional rooms, special considerations, box count, storage needs, additional stops, access concerns (elevator/parking/HOA — relevant since it's an apartment), or asked about moving stressors

3_pricing: no 'pricing is super simple' opener, never explained what's included (gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap pads, tools), no packing price detail, and skipped No Worries Damage Coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee, and the no-hidden-fees pitch entirely
4_clock: never explained when the clock starts on-site, the 15-minute prorated increments after the minimum, or did a sense-check

5_estimate: never mentioned truck count, and none of the estimate variables (stairs, specialty items, additional stops, drive time, packing time, walk distance, equivalents, traffic) were used to explain the 5-7 hour range or the packing request's effect on it
6_save_your_ass: entire prep speech skipped — no shorter-move-lower-bill framing, no consolidation examples, no carload tip

7_quote_booking: never attempted to lock in a date, never mentioned no deposit required, never offered an email confirmation or bolded detail recap, no 'any other questions' close, no hours/contact info given
8_politeness: never used the customer's name once on the call
9_bonus: no rapport-building or humor, no insurance explanation, FAQs were answered reactively rather than raised proactively, no budget-conscious framing
top_strength: Roselyn moved fast to a real number when asked — she broke down the weekend vs. weekday hourly tiers ($109 vs $102 per mover) and landed on a concrete estimate: "for a three bedroom appointment normally it would take five to seven hours... that would be $1,526." She also stayed patient through the customer's rapid-fire date-checking without getting flustered.
coaching_note: You quoted a price before you had the job — no address, no stairs, no elevator, nothing about what's being moved. On an apartment move, access and stairs change the estimate, and you need that before you give a number. You also never said the customer's name once, skipped the whole differentiator pitch (No Worries coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee), and let the call end without trying to lock in a date or offering to send a confirmation email. Slow down, probe first, then price — and always try to close before you hang up.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and patient throughout with a warm "happy Sunday" sign-off, but transactional and scripted-feeling overall — no name use, no empathy statements, mechanical topic jumps.
